newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ growth to peak at 4.3 pct in 1998/99 - NZIER.
newsitem.headline: NZ growth to peak at 4.3 pct in 1998/99 - NZIER.

text.p: The New Zealand Institute of Economic Research on Friday predicted economic growth would peak at 4.3 percent in 1998/99, driven by household spending.
Its previous forecasts, finalised in December before the formation of the new National/New Zealand First coalition government, saw 1998/99 GDP growth at 3.1 percent.
Changes to economic and fiscal policy, combined with revisions to historical GDP figures from Statistics NZ, were behind the altered growth forecasts, the independent NZIER said.
The Reserve Bank would be likely to respond by raising interest rates, it said.
The institute forecasts interest rates to remain around their current "low level" over 1997 with monetary conditions unchanged and inflation falling due to a slowing economy.
In 1998 inflation is seen rising due to higher government spending and looming tax cuts and monetary conditions will tighten.

Interest rates rise significantly as the Reserve Bank acts to stop inflation getting close to the top of its 3.0 percent target band. Rates are forecast to stay high for a time before falling from mid 1988.
NZIER said its forecasts had been finalised before the coalition government's March 4 Budget Policy Statement, which reshuffled planned additional government spending between years.

"Overall, the government still intends to spend an additional $5 billion over the next three years," the NZIER said, adding that the changes would have little impact on its outlook for economic growth.

It now sees GDP growth rising to 2.7 percent in 1997/98 (previously 3.3 percent) from 2.0 percent in 1996/97. After peaking at 4.3 percent in 1998/99 growth is seen easing to 3.3 percent in the March 2000 year and 2.9 percent in 2001.
The key changes to economic policy that had occurred after the NZIER's last predictions were:
* The $1.1 billion income tax cuts scheduled for July 1, 1997, were postponed for a year.
* Planned government spending in the 1997/98 June year was increased.
It saw growth among New Zealand's major trading partners remaining steady, averaging 3.8 percent over the forecast period.
